entries.requirement: Every assertive business statement you write or report (price, savings, demand, conversion, what customers said, results) must cite a fact from a system of record; if no fact exists, the claim stays absent and the reason for its absence is recorded.
entries.why: A structural check passes a fabricated claim because a false claim is well-formed; only an evidence gate looks at content.

origin.quote: **A claim about the world needs a fact. Absence stays absent.**

entries.requirement: Never let a modelled or projected figure fill a slot whose meaning is 'this was true': a projection, anchor price or forecast conversion rate is not an observed value, and only observed data may be reported as a result.
entries.why: A modelled anchor price presented as a former price is a false statement even when the model is sound.

origin.quote: - **Never let a recommendation become a fact.** A modelled anchor price is not a former

entries.requirement: Every monetary amount you record or compute carries its currency, scale and basis as fields; amounts without them are not added, compared or divided with other amounts.
entries.why: Combining amounts that differ in currency, scale or basis yields a number that looks precise and means nothing.

entries.requirement: Do not send, post or schedule any message to a customer, prospect or other person from a business round without an explicit owner approval bound to the exact message content; prepare it as a draft and stop.
entries.why: A message to a person is a mutation that cannot be taken back.

entries.requirement: If the work can spend, send, publish or mutate third-party state for more than one business, decide each effect from that business's own recorded authorization; a process-wide setting may only cap it, never grant it.
entries.why: Process-global mutable state cannot represent two businesses that legitimately hold different permissions.

origin.quote: - A process-global control is legitimate as a **ceiling** (a fleet-wide emergency stop)
